newsitem.title: GERMANY: German engineering output to rise 3 pct in 97 - VDMA.
newsitem.headline: German engineering output to rise 3 pct in 97 - VDMA.

text.p: German plant and machinery new orders fell six percent in real terms in 1996 while output grew one percent, the VDMA engineering industry association told Reuters on Wednesday.

Also, engineering output is likely to rise three percent in 1997, boosted by rising exports and by a possible pickup in domestic investment, which remains sluggish, VDMA chief economist Herbert Kriegbaum said in a telephone interview.
Kriegbaum said that in 1996, pan-German domestic engineering orders fell nine percent while orders from abroad fell four percent.
But order levels from abroad remained "quite acceptable" while domestic order levels were modest, Kriegbaum said.

He said the foreign order inflow was held back last year by the after-effects of the mark's appreciation in 1995 and by weak economic growth in western Europe, which accounts for almost half of German plant and equipment exports.
"Domestically, investment activity stagnated but deliveries weren't that badly affected thanks to an order overhang from 1995," Kriegbaum said.
"We think 1997 will be better, particularly because the world economy is doing better and west Europe is at the start of an economic recovery," Kriegbaum said.
Also the recent depreciation of the mark should boost the sector's ability to compete internationally, he added.
While there was no sign of rising domestic investment activity at present, the VDMA saw a chance that rising exports could fuel domestic investment this year.
Interest rates were low, wage deals for 1997 and beyond are moderate and increasing exports should raise capacity utilisation in exporting industries, Kiegbaum said.
"Those are all positive signals which should lead to an upward correction in investment plans," Kriegbaum said.
The VDMA expects engineering exports to grow by a real four percent in 1997 with domestic demand rising two percent, Kriegbaum said.
The industry last year generated sales of approximately 235 billion marks and employed some 945,000 people in November.
